advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make CutoverOutcome.failure_scope a single consistent type across both branches (either both FailureScope enum or both str).
evidence: pass_fuse.py:162 `scope=FailureScope.endpoint.value` — FuseDecision.scope is the str value, not the enum
operation_outcome.py:42-53 FailureScope is a str-Enum, so `FailureScope.endpoint == 'endpoint'` is True, masking the divergence in equality but not in isinstance/type checks
advisory.finding: CutoverOutcome.failure_scope carries two different types depending on the branch: a FailureScope enum member on the record path (outcome.failure_scope) but a plain str on the defer path (decision.scope, which is FailureScope.endpoint.value / 'endpoint'). Consumers comparing failure_scope against a FailureScope enum will behave inconsistently across the two paths.
scenarios: A downstream consumer doing `outcome.failure_scope is FailureScope.endpoint` (identity) or isinstance checks would treat the two branches differently

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject (or document/support) overrides that route a non-NON_CREATE_FAMILIES action such as 'create' onto COORDINATOR_ROUTE.
evidence: batch_dispatch.py:206-212 only checks `route not in (COORDINATOR_ROUTE, LEGACY_ROUTE)`; `route_for('create', {'create': 'coordinator'})` returns 'coordinator'
Commit message: 'defaulting the six non-create families to the S3 T1 coordinator' — create is intended to stay legacy
advisory.finding: route_for validates the override route string but not the family: an explicit override can route the 'create' family (which is deliberately excluded from NON_CREATE_FAMILIES) onto COORDINATOR_ROUTE, sending creates through the non-create coordinator path the design states must never handle create.
scenarios: An operator override map that names 'create' (typo or misuse) silently routes creates into the coordinator/fuse pipeline that is only specified for non-create families

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a coordinate_and_fuse test where two distinct scopes open (and/or one decision defers multiple tickets) asserting report.fuse_decisions ordering and dedup.
evidence: Added lines: `decision = cutover.fuse_decision` / `if decision is not None and id(decision) not in seen:` / `seen.add(id(decision))` / `fuse_decisions.append(decision)` build the deduped first-seen list.
Every cutover test asserts only `report.fuse_decisions == ()` (test_operation_coordinator.py:838, :1106) or `len(report.fuse_decisions) == 1` (:903) — no test opens two distinct scopes.

Named violating input: a plan set where jira/endpoint-a exhausts (opening an endpoint fuse deferring a matching ticket) AND a second independent endpoint/provider also opens its own fuse deferring another matching ticket would yield two entries in report.fuse_decisions; the ordering and the `id(decision) not in seen` dedup branch are untested against it.
advisory.finding: coordinate_and_fuse's fuse-decision aggregation (first-seen ordering plus the id(decision) dedup on report.fuse_decisions) is never exercised by a test with more than one distinct fuse decision, so a regression in the dedup/ordering logic would go undetected.
scenarios: Two independent scopes both open in one pass and each defer remaining matching work.
The same FuseDecision object is attached to multiple deferred outcomes (dedup branch).

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure deferred_count/skipped_count from build_pass_tally are reflected (or explicitly reconciled) in _persist_and_log so applied+failed+deferred+skipped accounts for every mutation.
evidence: reconcile.py:733-734 `mutations_applied = int(apply_tally.get("applied_count", 0))` / `mutation_failures = int(apply_tally.get("failed_count", 0))` — deferred_count and skipped_count are never consulted
This surface's coordinate_and_fuse is the first tally producer that can legitimately emit nonzero deferred (fuse-held remaining work) counts
blocking.finding: build_pass_tally emits deferred_count/skipped_count, but the LIVE consumer reconcile._persist_and_log reads only applied_count and failed_count from apply_tally; a cutover pass with deferred (fuse-held) or skipped mutations therefore has mutations_applied + mutation_failures < mutation_count, so those mutations silently disappear from the pass accounting.
scenarios: A cutover pass where the fuse opens an endpoint and defers remaining matching work: deferred tickets are neither applied nor failed, so 'applied N of N' under-counts and the deferred work is invisible in the persisted result
